contract_reconciliation: Final schema defaults cover all26core entries, including fixed10/722, and all51explicit radio forms while retaining the generic family fallback.

Parrot_enable/parrot_disable/echo_telemetry defaults now use protected=true to mirror their intrinsic admin requirement. Native core has no per-mapping protected field; false is only absence of additional mapping gate.

Keep radio aliases protected=false because native radio access policy is dynamic and six query variants public. Never gate the entire family or all mutations using a blanket true that breaks Open policy.
Parameters belong only to dispatch runtime. Persist no parameter field in mappings. Each parameterized radio decoder supplies the missing canonical typed fields using the documented raw tail grammar.
All exact radio spellings reject nonempty parameter. Variable selectors preserve leading zero spelling; 9970,99700,etc all mean priority off, so do not add a separate9970 prefix alias.

No code-defined ordinary mapping exists beyond26 table entries plus remote payloads, source-local escape/target semantics and configured macro triggers. Phone grammar forms are classified separately as inert foundation.

completion_audit.audit_scope: Read-only native-code reconciliation; no design/schema edits.

summary.proposed_scalar_status: New user-requested configurability; 3000 preserves the current hardcoded duration. Positive integer minimum 1 is a new contract decision, not existing native parser bounds.
summary.unkey_completion: Already implemented for ordinary local RF commands; source-specific peer exceptions remain.

findings.detail: CommandCollector finishes a nonempty active buffer on NUL only when wrapping(now_ms-last_ms)>=3000. This yields command text, then DtmfCommands.complete_command parses/authorizes it; unknown/invalid/incomplete handlers yield no operation.

All duration sites are hardcoded 3000, so configurability must reach all relevant owners, not only one collector. RF publisher emits one NUL after quiet time. DtmfCommands maintains per-source digit deadlines. PeerLink tracks its own deadline and PeerSession injects '#' on expiry. PhoneDtmfGrammar has a separate three-second tick.

evidence.meaning: Peer timeout currently synthesizes literal hash

findings.detail: RF publisher resets last_ms and arms timeout after every completed decoded digit including '#'; unkey or an emitted timeout disarms it. Control-side digit_deadline is renewed for 0-9/A-D/*; '#', NUL, Unkey and Lost clear it. Collector last_ms resets on initiating/restart '*', then on each accepted nonterminator digit. Phone grammar calls tick before incoming digit, then last_ms=max(last_ms,now_ms).

evidence.meaning: Collector restart and last accepted digit

findings.detail: Elapsed milliseconds, not wall/civil time. Current RF callbacks calculate now_ms=origin_ms+elapsed_samples/48 at 48 kHz; origin_ms is monotonic process epoch elapsed at activation. Peer session clocks use Instant epoch elapsed in milliseconds; host processes peer Digit with control clock.now_ms and retains captured RemoteUnkey timestamp.

An actual receiving falling edge emits Unkey after decoded digits for that frame. Ordinary local command collection maps Unkey directly to '#' and completes immediately; selected-remote mode ignores Unkey. New no-prefix collector should retain unkey as a completion event, independent of which literal terminator is configured.

evidence.meaning: Ordinary Unkey to completion, selected remote exception

findings.detail: Actual peer unkey currently completes ONLY remote-base family collection on that ingress, not ordinary peer commands or selected *4 forwarding. This is a native scope difference to preserve deliberately or change explicitly, not infer from local RF behavior. Peer and private phone collectors are isolated by origin and exact reply connection; phone entry requires authenticated matching PhoneSource.

evidence.meaning: Peer and authenticated phone digit entry
Origin plus exact connection keyed collectors
Independent expiry and remote-base-only peer unkey

findings.detail: In selected remote-command mode a literal '#' clears selection and emits no forwarded digit. Other 0-9/A-D/* symbols forward immediately. NUL timeout and Unkey do not clear selection in DtmfCommands. PeerSession's synthetic '#' timer can therefore have different semantics than NUL on a peer-origin selected collector; changing configurable terminator should not conflate completion events with literal hash or blindly move this behavior.

evidence.meaning: Selection survives unkey and NUL, exits on hash

findings.detail: PadTest is local human RF-only. It captures every valid keypad digit, including '*' and '#'; inactivity/NUL does not finish. Only actual Unkey ends capture and yields report. First 127 symbols retained, later symbols discarded with overflowed=true. Lost cancels capture entirely.

evidence.meaning: Capture hash, timeout, loss, bounds and peer tests

findings.detail: Native command collector accepts 127 symbols excluding initiating star and hash. On symbol 128 or invalid symbol it sets active=false, producing no operation; later digits cannot execute the retained prefix. A future '*' restarts and clears digits. It does not have the new contract's explicit ignore-until-next-completion overflow latch. Queue is 256 DigitEvents; overflow discards observed queued prefix and emits Lost, which resets collector and pad and cancels macro.

evidence.meaning: Lost cancels macro and resets collection

findings.detail: Native '*' is a global start/restart token except within recognized remote-base family arguments. Bare digits are ignored locally and may regenerate from idle peers. Mapping prefixes only allow 0-9/A-D, max 63; empty mapping disables that action. Collector may dispatch unambiguous complete fixed commands or macro trigger immediately on exact match, before hash/unkey/timeout. The new no-prefix candidate-buffer design with '*' or '#' literal inside mappings and boundary-only longest matching is an explicit behavior change.

evidence.meaning: Empty mappings disabled; typed argument parse
Star initiator and exact immediate dispatch

findings.detail: Native Asterisk execute_digits validates the full alphabet then appends# if absent and uses the shared RF collector through the product API with now_ms=0. Native macro compilation instead requires explicitly terminated commands and rejects incomplete tails. The proposed isolated execute_dtmf action is distinct: explicit delimiters complete immediately and a pending tail waits for configured inactivity within the whole invocation budget; no implicit# or fake RF unkey is inserted.

evidence.meaning: execute_digits appends hash and Incomplete result
Only explicit hash adds macro step

findings.detail: dtmf_admin_timeout_ms is 300000 by default, parsed from 1..u64::MAX in node/general settings. It controls authorization grant expiry; successful admin operations renew it. It is not command inactivity timeout and must remain separate.

contract_guidance: Add a scalar inactivity_timeout_ms beside terminator and mappings; default 3000 ms reflects current elapsed duration, but the scalar name and bounds are new design choices.
Retain RF unkey completion as mandatory behavior with no new enable/disable toggle.
Treat explicit terminator, inactivity, and actual unkey as distinguishable completion causes; do not implement inactivity/unkey by inventing literal '#'.

Declare live ingress and execute_dtmf end-of-string semantics separately: authorized synthetic action has no RF receiver-unkey and must wait for configured inactivity for a pending tail, within the invocation budget.
Describe no-prefix and boundary-only dispatch as deliberate redesign; native current behavior still requires '*' and permits immediate exact dispatch.
Preserve RF-only pad-test unkey semantics and current source/loss isolation unless user explicitly requests a change.
Do not claim all peer unkey paths already execute ordinary commands; current peer behavior is narrower.

contract_notes: All canonical command strings are complete codes. Legacy initiating star and provider family prefix are import/default inputs, not new special command-prefix syntax.
Generic radio fallback is retained for unknown/malformed radio payload handling. Explicit radio mappings are normal independent bindings; changing one does not silently rewrite others.

Provider default family is6/accesslocked and installed only with a configured enabled owner. Canonical authoring may retain all radio mappings while effective registration is dormant without that owner.
Use the actual legacy provider prefix to generate full radio codes during import; explicit canonical edits are then ordinary mapping updates.
Fixed radio spellings require empty parameter. Priority997 remains one parameterized mapping so0/00/etc all mean off without a longest-prefix collision.
Parrot/Echo telemetry defaults setprotectedtrue; radio false preserves public queries and configurable Open/Locked/Disabled mutation policy.
No built-in code is invented for DisconnectAll/ReconnectAll, typed runtime-only controls, inert phone grammar or arbitrary configured macro triggers.
New configurable inactivity timeout defaults3000ms. Unkey/timeout are completion reasons, not injected#; prior no-prefix/boundary-only/genericparameter requirements remain.
Code-derived native coverage remains77; the designed rx_mute_toggle *99 phone-only binding brings canonical defaults to78. It is not claimed to exist in the audited source.
